solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maraschino cocktail lacked no ability to impress

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the liqueur's name are mixed up
lacked means went without, so the word no is taken out of the liqueur's name

explanation.surface: A Maraschino cocktail that failed to impress anyone at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacked no' removes NO from MARASCHINO, leaving MARASCHI, which 'cocktail' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is the personal magnetism that lets someone impress and win over others.

clue.text: Smell American appetiser

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A smelly American starter dish.
explanation.walkthrough: HUMUS is a recognised variant spelling of hummus, the chickpea dip served as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hummus, the chickpea dip, is commonly served as a starter before a meal.

clue.text: These letters could be dreariest, on purpose

indicators.note: says the letters of the next words could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: A remark that some letters, rearranged, would read as the dreariest thing, said deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' looks like a single phrase meaning deliberately, but 'on' is fodder and 'purpose' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason for being, the French phrase, is the central purpose of a person or thing.

clue.text: Regal route had mushroom colour

indicators.note: had means held, so the abbreviation for a route contains the mushroom

parts.note: ST, street, is a route
a cep is a porcini mushroom
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A royal procession route painted in a mushroom shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing a sceptre, the royal staff, marks a person or realm as royal.

clue.text: Uncontrollable wolf eats a lone gnu without good camouflage

indicators.note: camouflage disguises a thing's appearance, so the letters are disguised by rearrangement
without means lacking, so the letter for good is dropped from gnu

explanation.surface: A wild wolf eats a solitary gnu that lacked decent cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' looks like a container signal but is fodder; GNU minus G leaves NU, and all the letters together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone answerable only to their own rules behaves independently and cannot be controlled by others.

clue.text: Seal bone in cupboard

parts.note: to seal something is to close it
T as in T-bone, the steak cut named after its T-shaped bone

explanation.surface: A seal bone tucked away in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' reads as the animal, but it is the verb to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small storage room or cupboard, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Temperamental supercomputer captures twp bytes

indicators.note: captures means holds inside, so the computer's name surrounds the letters

parts.note: Cray is a famous brand of supercomputer
twp is a typo for two; B is the abbreviation for byte, so two bytes gives BB

explanation.surface: A moody supercomputer swallows a couple of bytes of data.
explanation.definitionFit: A crabby person is bad-tempered and irritable, given to moods.

clue.text: Eggs are in round state

parts.note: O is round in shape
VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

explanation.surface: A claim that eggs exist in a circular condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the plural of ovum, the biological term for an egg cell.

clue.text: Extension to bank carries compiler remarkably

parts.note: EXT is the abbreviation for extension, as on a phone number

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the word for bank surrounds the setter

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
the compiler, the crossword setter, refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A bank's building extension supports the compiler in a notable way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean to an unusual or very great degree.

clue.text: Without apron, spill head of lime drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the remaining letters sit around the apron
spilling the head of a word throws away its first letter

parts.note: a bib is the top part of an apron

explanation.surface: Without an apron, someone spills the top of a lime drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here: IME (lime with its first letter spilled) goes round BIB.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to take in liquid, a formal way of saying to drink.

clue.text: Cut and paste at a clear menu

indicators.note: cutting and pasting moves text around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Editing instructions for a menu: cut and paste so it reads clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: An a la carte menu lists each dish priced separately, so the phrase names that kind of menu.

clue.text: It restrains hooligan who has bomb concealed

indicators.note: concealed means held out of sight inside the words that precede it

explanation.surface: A hooligan caught carrying a bomb under his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO is an Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a British court order restricting a troublemaker's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: The British court order is used to curb the behaviour of yobs and troublemakers.

clue.text: One used to torture general's army

parts.note: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of a tiny performer in P T Barnum's circus
a crew is a band of people, likened to an army

explanation.surface: A general's troops are used to torture prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw device crushing the thumbs was a medieval instrument of torture.

clue.text: Infections run rampant, though confined to refrigerator

indicators.note: confined means shut in, so the word to is held between the other pieces

parts.note: colds are common viral infections
to rage is to run rampant, as a fire or disease does
taken as written

explanation.surface: Infections spread wildly even though kept chilled in a fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' seems to belong with 'confined to refrigerator', but it is the inserted piece; 'confined' sits it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold store or refrigerated room keeps food chilled, the job a fridge does.

clue.text: Draw a straight flush

parts.note: dead means straight or directly, as in dead ahead
a flush is a rush of heat to the face

explanation.surface: A poker player draws a straight flush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straight flush' is a poker hand, but the words split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A race finishing level with no winner is a tie, a draw.

clue.text: Mysterious variations precede muscular spasm

indicators.note: precede puts the first piece before the spasm

parts.note: Elgar's Enigma Variations, the orchestral work
a tic is an involuntary muscular twitch

explanation.surface: Musical variations played before a muscle twitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enigmatic is puzzling and hard to interpret, so mysterious.

clue.text: Ogle king during speech

indicators.note: during speech means the name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic monarch

explanation.surface: A king leering at someone while giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle and to leer both mean to look at someone lustfully.

clue.text: The charm of Europe is up my street, with intelligence above all

indicators.note: in a down answer, intelligence's letters stand above everything else that follows

parts.note: IQ, intelligence quotient, measures intelligence

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: EU, the European Union, stands for Europe

explanation.surface: Someone says the allure of Europe suits them perfectly, especially its intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up my street' looks like the idiom for something one likes, but 'up' belongs with Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystique is an air of mystery and glamour that makes something charming.

clue.text: Stand up and join lots in alternate positions

indicators.note: only the letters in every other place are taken, starting from the first

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand and join several groups by turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone up, failing to meet them, is to jilt them.

clue.text: Agreed to go back on board ship with headless corpse for adventures

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a body is a corpse

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the reversed word sits between its letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a ship

indicators.note: go back means read in reverse order

parts.note: yes says agreed

explanation.surface: A crew agrees to return aboard a ship carrying a beheaded body for their adventures.
explanation.definitionFit: An odyssey is a long eventful journey, after Homer's epic of Odysseus's wanderings.

clue.text: Lauding missing daughter's cooked tongue

indicators.note: cooked means tampered with, so the letters are rearranged
missing means lacking, so the letter for daughter is removed

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone praising a missing daughter's cooked ox tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUDING less D leaves LAUING, which 'cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingua is Latin for tongue and is used for a language, as in lingua franca.

clue.text: I am bound to earn some money in opposition

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: to earn means to take in, so the word for confined takes in the coin

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means confined or bound
a dime is a US ten-cent coin, some money

explanation.surface: Someone says they are obliged to earn money despite resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstacle that stands in the way, a form of opposition.

clue.text: Just above line next to vertical axis

parts.note: on means above, resting upon
y is the vertical axis on a graph

explanation.surface: A point just above a line, beside a graph's vertical axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only both mean merely, nothing more than.

clue.text: Stick to Latin greetings

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: An instruction to stick to Latin when greeting people.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick used as a weapon in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian bamboo staff, often iron-tipped and used by police, is a kind of stick.

clue.text: Deviant wears leather-tipped gag

indicators.note: wears means holds on itself, so the strange word takes in the letter

parts.note: deviant means strange, odd
the tip of leather is its first letter, L

explanation.surface: A deviant wearing a leather-tipped gag.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone can mean to choke or throttle them, as to strangle does.

clue.text: Otherwise some English people express alarm

indicators.note: many English speakers drop a final r, so the spoken word comes out sounding like another

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in hurry or you'll miss it

explanation.surface: Some English people express alarm in a different way.
explanation.walkthrough: OR said without its R sounds like the answer, as in non-rhotic southern English.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential fear and dread, so a kind of alarm.

clue.text: In pursuit of unknown amount of liquid crystal

indicators.note: in pursuit of puts the unknown after the measure, chasing it

parts.note: a quart is a liquid measure, a quarter of a gallon
z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Chasing an unknown amount of liquid crystal.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is loose: Z follows QUART, so Z is the one in pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartz is a crystalline mineral, silica, often found as clear crystals.

clue.text: Outline he sculptured briefly on skirt and angora top

parts.note: sc is short for sculpsit, Latin for he sculptured, as carved on statues
to skirt is to border or edge, to hem

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sculptor briefly outlines a skirt and an angora top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sc.' (sculpsit) appears on statues and engravings beside the artist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is a diagram or plan giving the outline of something.

clue.text: Wild, loud Frenchman had little time to speak

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
Rene is a French man's name

indicators.note: to speak means the word is said, giving one sounding the same

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a little time

explanation.surface: A loud Frenchman with barely a moment to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frantic, wildly excited.
